t: The leading principality of north-eastern Rus’, ruled from Vladimir on the Klyazma after Andrei Bogolyubsky made it his capital in 1157.
Its white-stone churches and the icon of Our Lady of Vladimir became lasting symbols of Russian culture.
After the Mongol conquest of 1238 its grand-princely title was granted by the khans and finally passed to Moscow.
dyk: The icon of Our Lady of Vladimir, painted in Constantinople in the early 12th century, was brought north by Andrei Bogolyubsky in 1155 and is now in Moscow’s Tretyakov Gallery.
ev: Andrei Bogolyubsky becomes prince and makes Vladimir his capital
Andrei Bogolyubsky is murdered at Bogolyubovo
Vsevolod the Big Nest rules as grand prince
Battle of Lipitsa between Vsevolod’s sons
The Mongols sack Vladimir and kill Yuri II on the Sit River
Ivan I Kalita of Moscow becomes sole grand prince
